title: Diagnose the Codex and Vercel toolchain

bridge.applicationConcept: Codex context, local CLIs, deployment inspection, and evidence boundaries
bridge.analogyLimit: A CLI may have write privileges and cloud credentials; it is not inherently a read-only management plane.

buildBrief: Complete a tool-access matrix, add project AGENTS.md guidance, deploy the practice app, and use Codex plus Vercel CLI evidence to explain the deployment state.
incidentBrief: The preview build receives a deliberately missing public configuration name. Diagnose the build log, distinguish build-time from runtime state, and make the smallest safe correction.

scenario.symptoms: The preview reports a missing NEXT_PUBLIC training variable and shows which phase read it.

acceptanceTests: Codex reports the intended repository instructions
The tool matrix separates read, write, authentication, sensitive data, and revocation
The deployment diagnosis cites a specific safe log line and focused diff
predictionQuestions: Which tool can observe the deployment and which can mutate it?
At what phase is each environment value read?
defenseQuestions: Explain why Codex must start in the correct repository.
Compare a CLI, API, SDK, plugin, MCP server, and documentation site.
Identify one tool permission you would revoke after the exercise.
hints: Ask each tool what it can read, write, and authenticate to.
Search the first relevant build error rather than the final generic failure line.
Match the variable name and environment before changing application code.
